gap: No result ChatGPT got states that SoundGuys measured 88 h 27 min of playback at 75 dB on the Logitech G Pro X 2 LIGHTSPEED, against Logitech's 'up to 50 hours' claim and about twice the 42 h 10 min SoundGuys measured on the Arctis Nova 5X. None states that SoundGuys measured 200–250 ms of lag on the G Pro X 2 over Bluetooth.
standout_why: Compared against these pages: (1) the cited SoundGuys roundup (updated 2026-09-09) lists the G Pro X 2 only as a notable mention with no figures, though it does give the Nova 5X's 'over 42 h' on 2.4 GHz, so the Nova 5X half of the finding is already there. (2) Modima Labs (2026-10-20) says it did no hands-on testing and gives only Logitech's 50 h claim. (3) RTINGS' gaming roundup, Tom's Guide and the cited GamesRadar page returned no body text through the fetch tool, so I could not check them. ChatGPT's own answer repeats the 60 h claim for the Nova 5X and gives no battery or latency figure for the G Pro X 2.
decides: This keeps the split ChatGPT made but adds measured reasons for it. If someone plays on PC or PS5, the G Pro X 2 lasted about 2× longer between charges than the Nova 5X in SoundGuys' tests (88.5 h vs 42.2 h). On Xbox, though, it works only over the 3.5 mm cable (SoundGuys), and its 200–250 ms Bluetooth lag is too slow for gaming. So for one wireless headset across PC plus Xbox plus PS5, the Nova 5X stays the pick. SteelSeries lists Xbox Series X|S and PS5 for it, but buyers should expect about 42 h of battery, not the advertised 60 h.

findings.label: Measured battery life (SoundGuys)
findings.source_title: Logitech G PRO X 2 LIGHTSPEED review - SoundGuys
findings.note: SoundGuys continuous playback test at 75 dB(SPL). The page does not say which connection was used. Logitech claims 'up to 50 hours', so the measured figure is about 177% of the claim. The page shows 'Published Apr 10, 2025' and also says it was 'updated on December 12, 2023'. The byline runs together as 'Sam Moore Adam Birney'.

findings.label: Measured Bluetooth latency (SoundGuys)
findings.source_title: Logitech G PRO X 2 LIGHTSPEED review - SoundGuys
findings.note: Reviewer: 'I measured roughly 200-250ms of latency over Bluetooth'. Fine for video and music, but noticeably delayed for competitive gaming. The same review says the USB dongle is best for PC and PS5, works with a docked Switch but not other consoles, and that Xbox needs the 3.5 mm TRRS cable.

findings.note: 'Get up to 50 hours of use on a single charge', with no stated conditions. Connections: LIGHTSPEED, Bluetooth, 3.5 mm. Price on Logitech's US store today.

findings.label: Measured battery life (SoundGuys)
findings.source_title: SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5X review: One gaming headset to rule them all? - SoundGuys
findings.note: Connected to a PC through the USB-C dongle (the review says '2.5 GHz', which looks like a typo for 2.4 GHz), at about 50% volume. Against the 60 h headline that is about 70%. SoundGuys also reports 15 min of charging gave about 6 h of playback. By Adam Birney, published 2024-07-17, updated 2025-03-28. The cited SoundGuys roundup already gives 'over 42 h'.
